claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for?** If yes, how many children and what are their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child I'm looking to claim for. I have one child - Alex, who is 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few questions about Alex to assess eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, attending college, sixth form, or an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. 

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care?** (For example, do you provide for his needs such as food, clothes, and other day-to-day expenses?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for all of Alex's day-to-day needs - food, clothes, everything he needs really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just one final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Although Alex is 18 years old, he is still in approved education (studying for A-levels at sixth form college)
- Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 who remain in approved education or training
- You live in the UK, Alex lives with you, and you're responsible for his care
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him

You can continue to claim Child Benefit for Alex until he either:
- Turns 20, or
- Leaves approved education or training

**Please note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might need to pay back some or all of it through your tax return.

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If Alex's education status changes (such as if he leaves sixth form or completes his A-levels), you should inform HMRC.

The claimant lives in the UK (Manchester), Alex lives with them, the claimant is responsible for Alex's care and provides for his day-to-day needs (food, clothes, etc.), and nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex. All eligibility criteria are met.
